title: Juggling: What the Heck
summary: Josh and Chuck explain juggling, starting with a casual opening about trying to juggle and the history of juggling from ancient Egyptian tomb images and a Talmud reference to a rabbi who could juggle eight torches, through medieval jugglers, vaudeville, and the 1940s founding of juggling associations and the World Juggling Federation. They then give a beginner's walkthrough of three-ball cascade juggling (starting with one ball, the two-ball and three-ball steps, chasing the ball, learning against a wall), describe variations like the reverse cascade, shower, tricks, bounce juggling, clawing, cigar box and shaker cup juggling, club and ring juggling, contact ring juggling, and partner juggling (passing, stealing and replacing, combat juggling). The physics of juggling (gravity, parabolic paths, prop mass), Claude Shannon's juggling theorem, site swap notation, and vision research on juggling are covered. The episode closes with a listener mail story about Jennifer Grace and her husband Tom, who is hospitalized, and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter about juggling
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about juggling, Chuck's failed attempt to learn in an hour, and the episode's Jonathan Strickland-written source article.

segments.title: History of juggling
segments.summary: Juggling traced from ancient Egyptian tomb images and a Talmud reference to a rabbi juggling eight torches, through Greece, Rome, medieval performers, vaudeville (including W. C. Fields), and the 1940s formation of juggling groups and the International Juggling Association.

segments.title: Anthony Gatto and the juggling scene
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Anthony Gatto, a record-holding juggler who quit to run a concrete business, and a Grantland article about him, along with YouTube instructional videos by Adam Schomsky.

segments.title: Beginner equipment and three-ball cascade basics
segments.summary: Advice to start with bean bags, which do not roll away, and the terminology of props. Starting with one ball, then the two-ball and three-ball cascade, with a hand motion scooping in a figure eight and throws timed at half-beat intervals.

segments.title: Cascade variations and reverse cascade
segments.summary: The reverse cascade is described as the opposite hand direction, with Josh's law about which hand throws higher. Practice tips include juggling against a wall to avoid chasing balls.

segments.title: Juggling tricks and variations
segments.summary: Discussion of tricks such as the half shower, tennis move, Mills mess, Burke's barrage, and Ruben Stein's revenge; bounce juggling, clawing, and the chop; and bartender flair.

segments.title: Toss juggling with odd and even numbers; cigar box, shaker cups, clubs, rings
segments.summary: Odd and even prop counts and patterns (criss-cross, fountain, column, synchronous and asynchronous), then cigar box and shaker cup juggling, club shapes, and ring juggling and contact ring juggling.

segments.title: Partner juggling and combat juggling
segments.summary: Juggling as a social activity: passing patterns such as the three-three-ten, stealing and replacing, and combat juggling where players try to knock props from each other's hands.

segments.title: Physics, Shannon's theorem, site swap, and vision
segments.summary: Gravity and parabolic flight paths, why more props require higher throws, the effect of prop mass, Claude Shannon's juggling theorem, site swap notation, and research showing jugglers rely on feel and early flight-path vision.
